outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail: both status records have completed evaluations, solution_passed false, and 17/32 samples passed. The concrete difference is process shape, not outcome: serial used one coherent implementation path, while parallel wrote and reconciled competing deliverable trees before arriving at a locally verified implementation. The shared official failure count means the deliverable overwrite is retained only as a realized parallel coordination problem, not as a proven differential cause.
parallel_contributors: Parallel subagents created overlapping implementation artifacts and the parent cleaned the final tree after interruption.
Parallel local verification passed the visible sample and parser/byte checks but did not prevent the hidden official failures.
serial_contributors: Serial used a single actor and no delegation, avoiding shared write conflicts.
Serial local randomized and sample checks also missed the hidden official failures.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations likely share a hidden-case behavioral gap that is not identified by the available official summary.
Serial performed a 20-case randomized comparison that parallel did not reproduce at parent level, but both official scores were identical.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is parallel adverse process only
